name: Virgin
editorial_article: Virgin Records was a legendary British independent record label founded in 1972 that played a pivotal role in the development of progressive, experimental, and new wave music during the 1970s and 80s. Emerging from Richard Branson's successful Virgin Mail Order business and record shop chain, the label was co-founded by Branson and his cousin, Simon Draper, alongside Nik Powell. While Branson provided the entrepreneurial drive and public face for the burgeoning Virgin Group, it was Draper who took the aesthetic lead, utilizing his deep knowledge of imported progressive rock and experimental sounds to curate a roster that was both critically acclaimed and culturally significant. The label's early identity was built on an "audio Arts Council" model, funded largely by the massive commercial success of Mike Oldfield’s *Tubular Bells*. This unexpected hit allowed the label to pursue more avant-garde projects, including works by Can, Tangerine Dream, Faust, Gong, and Robert Wyatt. As the decade shifted, Virgin successfully navigated the punk and post-punk landscapes, signing seminal acts such as the Sex Pistols, The Human League, Public Image Ltd, Magazine, XTC, and Simple Minds. By the 1980s, Virgin had grown into a global powerhouse, though it eventually shifted from its independent, experimental roots, culminating in its acquisition and incorporation into larger music conglomerates. Despite its later commercialization, the label remains a touchstone for the innovative, risk-taking A&R philosophy of its foundational years, bridging the gap between underground experimentation and mainstream pop success.
